passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) is designed to provide a reader of 3M’s financial statements with a narrative from the perspective of management. 3M’s MD&A is presented in the following sections: • Overview • Results of Operations • Performance by Business Segment • Performance by Geographic Area • Critical Accounting Estimates • New Accounting Pronouncements • Financial Condition and Liquidity • Financial Instruments Forward-looking statements in Item 7 may involve risks and uncertainties that could cause results to differ materially from those projected (refer to the section entitled Cautionary Note Concerning Factors That May Affect Future Results in Item 1 and the risk factors provided in Item 1A for discussion of these risks and uncertainties). Additional information about results of operations and financial condition for 2024 and 2023 (including the detailed discussion of the prior year 2024 to 2023 year-over-year changes) can be found in Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations sections in 3M's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. Table of Contents Overview 3M is a diversified global manufacturer, technology innovator and marketer of a wide variety of products and services. As discussed in Note 1, certain changes are reflective in this document for all applicable periods presented. As discussed in Note 2, on April 1, 2024, 3M completed the separation of its Health Care business (the Separation) through a pro rata distribution of 80.1% of the outstanding shares of Solventum Corporation (Solventum) to 3M stockholders. As a result, Solventum became an independent public company, 3M no longer consolidated Solventum into 3M’s financial results and the historical net income of Solventum, and applicable assets and liabilities included in the Separation were reported in 3M's consolidated financial statements as discontinued operations. 3M manages its continuing operations in three operating business segments: Safety and Industrial; Transportation and Electronics; and Consumer. From a geographic perspective, EMEA refers to Europe, the Middle East, and Africa on a combined basis. Unless otherwise noted, any sales change analysis compares 2025 with 2024, year-on-year (YoY). passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Provided below is a cautionary discussion of what we believe to be the most important risk factors applicable to the Company. Discussion of these factors is incorporated by reference into and considered an integral part of Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.” Risks Related to the Global Economy and External Conditions * The Company’s results are impacted by the effects of, and changes in, worldwide economic, political, regulatory, international trade, geopolitical, tariffs and retaliatory counter measures, and other external conditions. During 2025, the Company derived approximately 56 percent of its revenues from outside the United States. Accordingly, the Company’s operations and the execution of its business strategies and plans are subject to global competition and economic and geopolitical risks that are beyond its control, such as, among other things, disruptions in financial markets, economic downturns, military conflicts, terrorism, public health emergencies, political changes and trends such as protectionism, economic nationalism resulting in government actions impacting international trade agreements or imposing trade restrictions such as tariffs and retaliatory counter measures, and government deficit reduction and other austerity measures in locations or industries in which the Company operates. Further escalation of specific trade tensions, including those between the U.S. and China, or more broadly in global trade conflict, could have a material adverse effect on the Company's business and operations around the world. The Company's business is also impacted by social, political, and labor conditions in locations in which the Company or its suppliers or customers operate; adverse changes in the availability and cost of capital; monetary policy; interest rates; inflation; recession; commodity prices; currency volatility or exchange control; ability to expatriate earnings; and other laws and regulations in the jurisdictions in which the Company or its suppliers or customers operate. For example, changes in local economic condition or outlooks, such as lower economic growth rates in China, Europe, or other key markets, impact the demand or profitability of the Company's products. The global economy has been impacted by geopolitical tensions. The U.S. and other governments have imposed, and propose to impose additional, export controls and tariffs on certain products, and financial and economic sanctions on certain industry sectors and parties. These geopolitical tensions could result in, among other things, cyberattacks, supply chain disruptions (including limitations on access to rare earth minerals and other raw materials), higher energy and other commodity costs, lower consumer demand, and changes to foreign exchange rates and financial markets, and tariffs and trade restrictions may result in increased production costs and product pricing, further supply chain disruptions, limited access to end markets, lower profitability, and uncertainty related to planning long-term investments and strategies, and may have other competitive effects. credit_strengths.text: MMM's gross leverage sits comfortably below the sector median, reflecting a conservative balance sheet relative to health care peers. The company's net leverage also remains below the sector median, indicating modest net debt after cash. This provides meaningful headroom against the next downgrade threshold, with EBITDA able to decline by roughly one-sixth before breaching the tier.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure and leaves positive free cash flow, though the cash conversion ratio trails the sector median. Interest coverage remains adequate, with operating income covering interest expense multiple times. The current ratio exceeds the sector median, suggesting solid near-term liquidity. These factors support the capacity to service debt from internally generated funds.

key_risks.text: The debt note discloses that a significant portion of long-term debt matures within the next twelve months, with the current portion of long-term debt representing a material refinancing need. Additionally, the company terminated swaps that had converted fixed-rate notes to floating-rate, potentially increasing exposure to interest rate volatility. These features warrant monitoring of refinancing conditions and funding costs.

The risk factors highlight that MMM derives a majority of revenues from outside the United States, exposing it to tariffs, trade restrictions, and geopolitical tensions. Escalation of trade conflicts, particularly between the U.S. and China, could disrupt supply chains, raise costs, and reduce demand. This external vulnerability may pressure operating cash flow and, consequently, debt servicing capacity.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow to debt is modest, and the cash flow coverage ratio is below the sector median, indicating weaker cash-based debt servicing relative to peers. However, interest coverage remains adequate, and the company retains substantial cash balances. The maturity profile shows a manageable near-term refinancing need, but the company must continue generating sufficient cash to meet obligations.

MMM's free cash flow is insufficient to cover shareholder distributions, with dividends and buybacks exceeding free cash flow. This shortfall may require drawing on cash balances or incremental borrowing, potentially weakening the debt servicing capacity over time. The company's ability to sustain distributions while servicing debt depends on improving operating cash flow.

overall_credit_view.text: MMM presents an intermediate financial risk profile, with leverage below the sector median but cash flow coverage weaker than peers. The company's diversified business and substantial cash position support credit quality, yet the elevated shareholder distributions and near-term maturities require careful monitoring. The indicative profile is not a rating, but suggests a stable credit outlook.

Analyst judgement: MMM's credit metrics are expected to remain supported by its global franchise and cost management, but external trade risks and refinancing needs could pressure metrics. The company's ability to generate consistent operating cash flow and manage its maturity profile will be key to maintaining its current risk profile. We view the credit as stable but sensitive to cash flow volatility.

credit_strengths.text: MMM的總槓桿率舒適地低於行業中位數，反映其資產負債表相對於醫療保健同業而言較為保守。公司的淨槓桿率亦維持在行業中位數以下，顯示扣除現金後的淨債務適度。這為應對下一個降級門檻提供了有意義的緩衝空間，EBITDA可在觸及該級別前下降約六分之一。
營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支並產生正自由現金流，儘管現金轉換率落後於行業中位數。利息覆蓋率維持充足，營運收入足以覆蓋利息開支多倍。流動比率高於行業中位數，顯示短期流動性穩健。這些因素支持其以內部產生資金償還債務的能力。

key_risks.text: 債務票據披露，長期債務中有相當部分將於未來十二個月內到期，其中長期債務的流動部分代表重大的再融資需求。此外，公司終止了將固定利率票據轉換為浮動利率的掉期，可能增加對利率波動的敞口。這些特徵值得監控再融資條件及融資成本。
風險因素強調，MMM的大部分收入來自美國以外地區，使其面臨關稅、貿易限制及地緣政治緊張局勢的風險。貿易衝突升級，尤其是美國與中國之間，可能擾亂供應鏈、推高成本並減少需求。此外部脆弱性可能對營運現金流構成壓力，進而影響償債能力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流對債務比率適度，現金流覆蓋率低於行業中位數，顯示相對於同業，其以現金為基礎的償債能力較弱。然而，利息覆蓋率維持充足，公司亦持有大量現金結餘。到期結構顯示短期再融資需求可控，但公司必須繼續產生足夠現金以履行義務。
MMM的自由現金流不足以覆蓋股東分派，股息及回購超過自由現金流。此缺口可能需要動用現金結餘或增量借貸，可能隨時間削弱償債能力。公司在償還債務的同時維持分派的能力，取決於營運現金流的改善。

overall_credit_view.text: MMM呈現中等財務風險狀況，槓桿率低於行業中位數，但現金流覆蓋率弱於同業。公司多元化的業務及龐大的現金狀況支持信貸質量，然而較高的股東分派及短期到期債務需要謹慎監控。指示性狀況並非評級，但暗示信貸展望穩定。
分析師判斷：預期MMM的信貸指標將繼續受到其全球業務網絡及成本管理所支持，但外部貿易風險及再融資需求可能對指標構成壓力。公司產生穩定營運現金流及管理其到期結構的能力，將是維持其當前風險狀況的關鍵。我們認為該信貸穩定，但對現金流波動敏感。
